text:
alex: quick follow-up to the rollout metadata RFC. i'd like to propose a very small, auditable hint that helps client-side resolvers prefer variants that are likely compatible when all other signals (latency/cost) are equal. sketch and ops notes below. please poke holes.

alex: fields (opt-in): `compat_v` (string, e.g. \"v0.2\"), `compat_score` (0-100, string), `token_schema_hash` (short hash). example: 
```
anchor: assistant-x@2026-10-01
compat_v: v0.2
compat_score: 82
token_schema_hash: b2:7f3e2a
note: score combines tokenizer-shape+cfg-sig; 100 = exact expected match
```

maria: i like numeric score instead of enum because it gives resolver a monotonic ordering and lets us tune small epsilons. ops questions: who computes score and hash?

josh: compute in onboarding pipeline (tokenizer + config fingerprint). score formula documented in registry. keep it conservative: only token/schema shape, not weights. default to 0/empty for legacy models.

carmen: safety: resolver MUST treat hint as tie-break only. server-side handshake remains authoritative. add feature flag so we can flip on gradually. also do not let hints affect pin eviction or autoscaler decisions.

alex: agreed. plan: resolver adds small epsilon based on compat_score when selecting among equal-cost nodes; pinned pools ignore score for eviction.

maria: telemetry suggestions: `hint.attempted`, `hint.favored`, `hint.conflict` with labels (model-version, route). track fraction of requests where hint changed selection.

josh: testing: unit tests for ordering, simulation with randomized incorrect scores (fuzz), and a canary routing 0.5% traffic. also add an eval job that periodically compares outputs between high-score variants to ensure score stays predictive.

carmen: migration/backfill: add fields nullable in schema, default existing to compat_v=null and compat_score=0; run a rate-limited backfill for catalog. provide a one-off CLI to recompute for a model-version for customer ops.

maria: storage note: token_schema_hash ~ 12 chars, compat_score tiny; indexing cost negligible. backfill CPU for tokenizer hashing is the bigger operational cost. plan low-priority background job during off-peak.

josh: security: expose only salted hashes (document salt policy). avoid any reversible identifiers. document hashing alg and make it explicit in schema.

carmen: pin nuance confirmed: hints are intra-bucket ordering only. add explicit test to ensure no evictions triggered by score.

alex: rollout plan summary: 1) schema nullable fields + compat_v versioning, 2) onboarding computes hint for new uploads, 3) backfill job for old entries (rate-limited), 4) resolver change behind feature flag using score as tie-break, 5) canary + telemetry for 2 weeks, then flip.

maria: add metrics dashboard before flipping. if `hint.conflict` > threshold, roll flag back.

meta-bot: ACTIONS: 1) alex -> draft schema diff text and sample client snippet. 2) josh -> onboarding compute spike + perf estimate. 3) maria -> telemetry dashboard + thresholds. 4) carmen -> validation that pin eviction ignores score. ETA EOW.

alex: thanks all — i'll post the schema PR link here when ready. :thumbsup:
